topics.label: Fallacies of Distributed Computing
topics.desc: The eight false assumptions (network is reliable, latency is zero, bandwidth is infinite, etc.) that doom naive distributed designs.

topics.label: Partial Failure
topics.desc: The defining hardship of distributed systems: some nodes fail while others continue, with no reliable way to tell which from outside.

topics.label: Failure Models
topics.desc: Taxonomy of failures—crash-stop, crash-recovery, omission, and Byzantine—that defines what guarantees an algorithm can possibly provide.

topics.label: CAP Theorem
topics.desc: Under a network partition a system must choose between consistency and availability—the canonical, if oversimplified, tradeoff framing.

topics.label: PACELC Theorem
topics.desc: Refines CAP: even absent partitions, systems trade latency against consistency, capturing the everyday cost CAP ignores.

topics.label: FLP Impossibility
topics.desc: Proves deterministic consensus is impossible in an asynchronous system with even one crash, motivating timeouts and randomization.

topics.label: Clocks & Time
topics.desc: Physical clock skew and drift make wall-clock time unreliable for ordering events, forcing logical or hybrid schemes across nodes.

topics.label: Happens-Before Relation
topics.desc: Lamport's partial causal order over events that underpins logical clocks and the very definition of causal consistency.

topics.label: Logical & Vector Clocks
topics.desc: Counters that order events by causality—scalar Lamport clocks for total order, vector clocks to detect true concurrency.

topics.label: Linearizability
topics.desc: The strongest single-object guarantee: operations appear instantaneous and in real-time order, making a system behave like one machine.

topics.label: Sequential Consistency
topics.desc: All processes observe one total operation order respecting per-process program order, but without real-time recency constraints.

topics.label: Causal Consistency
topics.desc: Guarantees causally related operations are seen in order everywhere while letting concurrent ones diverge, the strongest highly-available model.

topics.label: Eventual Consistency
topics.desc: Replicas converge given no new writes; maximizes availability and latency at the cost of reading stale or conflicting data.

topics.label: Session Guarantees
topics.desc: Client-centric promises—read-your-writes, monotonic reads, monotonic writes—that make eventual consistency tolerable per session.

topics.label: The Consensus Problem
topics.desc: Getting nodes to agree on one value despite failures, satisfying agreement, validity, and termination—the core of fault-tolerant coordination.

topics.label: Quorums
topics.desc: Overlapping majority sets (R+W>N) that guarantee any two operations intersect, the workhorse of consistency without full agreement.

topics.label: Paxos
topics.desc: The seminal crash-fault-tolerant consensus protocol using prepare/accept phases and quorums, notoriously subtle but foundational.

topics.label: Raft
topics.desc: An understandability-first consensus algorithm splitting leader election, log replication, and safety into clear, implementable modules.

topics.label: Leader Election
topics.desc: Selecting a single coordinator among peers to serialize decisions, with terms and fencing to prevent split-brain after failures.

topics.label: Byzantine Fault Tolerance
topics.desc: Consensus tolerating arbitrary, malicious nodes (PBFT-style), requiring 3f+1 replicas and underpinning permissioned blockchains.

topics.label: Coordination Services
topics.desc: Systems like ZooKeeper and etcd that expose consensus as primitives—locks, leader election, config—so apps avoid rolling their own.

topics.label: Replication Fundamentals
topics.desc: Keeping copies of data on multiple nodes for availability, latency, and read scaling—the source of every consistency tradeoff.

topics.label: Leader-Follower Replication
topics.desc: Writes go to one leader and stream to read-only followers; simple and common but the leader is a write bottleneck and failover risk.

topics.label: Multi-Leader Replication
topics.desc: Multiple writable replicas boost write availability across regions but introduce write conflicts demanding resolution strategies.

topics.label: Leaderless Replication
topics.desc: Dynamo-style quorum reads and writes to any replica, using read repair and anti-entropy to converge without a designated leader.

topics.label: Sync vs Async Replication
topics.desc: Whether the leader waits for follower acks trades durability and consistency against write latency and availability on failure.

topics.label: Partitioning & Sharding
topics.desc: Splitting a dataset across nodes by key range or hash so each holds a subset, the prerequisite for horizontal write scaling.

topics.label: Consistent Hashing
topics.desc: Maps keys and nodes onto a ring so adding or removing a node remaps only a small fraction of keys, with virtual nodes for balance.

topics.label: Message Queues
topics.desc: Async broker-mediated channels that decouple producers from consumers, smoothing load spikes and enabling independent scaling.

topics.label: Publish-Subscribe
topics.desc: Topic-based fan-out where many consumers each receive a message, decoupling senders from an unknown, dynamic set of receivers.

topics.label: Delivery Semantics
topics.desc: At-most-once, at-least-once, and exactly-once guarantees that dictate whether consumers must dedupe or tolerate message loss.

topics.label: Log-Based Streaming
topics.desc: Durable, ordered, replayable partitioned logs (Kafka-style) where consumers track offsets, unifying messaging and event storage.

topics.label: Stream Processing
topics.desc: Continuous computation over unbounded event streams with windowing, joins, and stateful operators for low-latency analytics.

topics.label: Backpressure & Flow Control
topics.desc: Signaling consumer capacity upstream so fast producers don't overwhelm slow consumers, preventing buffer blowup and collapse.

topics.label: Message Ordering
topics.desc: Preserving per-key order through partitioning while balancing parallelism, since global ordering kills throughput at scale.

topics.label: Distributed Transactions
topics.desc: Atomic commit spanning multiple nodes or services, the hardest distributed-data problem because failures can leave partial state.

topics.label: Two-Phase Commit
topics.desc: A coordinator's prepare-then-commit protocol giving atomicity across nodes, but blocking indefinitely if the coordinator fails.

topics.label: Saga Pattern
topics.desc: Replaces distributed transactions with a sequence of local transactions plus compensating actions, trading atomicity for availability.

topics.label: CRDTs
topics.desc: Conflict-free replicated data types whose merges are commutative and associative, guaranteeing convergence without coordination.

topics.label: Conflict Resolution
topics.desc: Reconciling concurrent writes via last-write-wins, vector-clock siblings, or app-defined merges—unavoidable with multi-writer replication.

topics.label: Anti-Entropy & Read Repair
topics.desc: Background reconciliation using Merkle trees plus on-read fixes that drive divergent replicas back toward agreement over time.

topics.label: Fault Tolerance Basics
topics.desc: Designing systems that keep working despite component failures through redundancy, isolation, and graceful degradation.

topics.label: Redundancy
topics.desc: Duplicating components or data so no single failure causes outage—the most basic and powerful resilience mechanism.

topics.label: Failure Detection
topics.desc: Heartbeats, timeouts, and phi-accrual detectors that infer node death despite never perfectly distinguishing it from slowness.

topics.label: Timeouts & Retries
topics.desc: Bounding waits and re-issuing failed calls with exponential backoff and jitter, the front line against transient faults.

topics.label: Idempotency
topics.desc: Designing operations safe to retry by deduplicating via keys, the property that makes at-least-once delivery and retries correct.

topics.label: Circuit Breaker
topics.desc: Tripping open after repeated failures to stop hammering a sick dependency, failing fast and giving it room to recover.

topics.label: Cascading Failures
topics.desc: Failures that propagate as retries and load shift onto survivors, the systemic collapse that bulkheads and load shedding exist to stop.

topics.label: Load Balancing
topics.desc: Distributing requests across replicas via round-robin, least-connections, or hashing to spread load and route around failures.

topics.label: Service Discovery
topics.desc: Letting services locate dynamic peer instances through a registry, replacing brittle static addresses in elastic deployments.

topics.label: Rate Limiting & Throttling
topics.desc: Token-bucket or sliding-window caps that protect services from overload and enforce fair multi-tenant resource sharing.

topics.label: Bulkhead Isolation
topics.desc: Partitioning resources into pools so one overloaded component can't exhaust threads or connections needed by the rest.

topics.label: Leader Lease & Fencing
topics.desc: Time-bounded leadership plus monotonic fencing tokens that stop a paused old leader from corrupting state after a new one takes over.

topics.label: Transactional Outbox
topics.desc: Writing events to a local DB table in the same transaction as state, then relaying them, to avoid dual-write inconsistency.

topics.label: Sidecar & Service Mesh
topics.desc: Offloading retries, mTLS, and telemetry to a colocated proxy so cross-cutting distributed concerns live outside app code.
